comparison: Both evaluations support the protein synthesis claims (C47-C52). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the multiple orthogonal methods and controls. Peer reviewers affirmed the method as 'solid and convincing' with no concerns raised about protein production data. Peer R1 also includes methodological claims C34-C36 that OpenEval addresses separately in R15.

Both address oligomeric assembly (C53-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantification and speculative interpretation, noting the signal is 'not as robust.' Peer reviewers initially raised concerns about mechanistic interpretation but ultimately SUPPORTED after new SEC experiments were performed, indicating acceptance of the assembly data despite OpenEval's reservations.

Both support the orientation data (C56-C59). OpenEval provides detailed analysis noting that only 38.5% showed correct orientation while acknowledging the method successfully identifies suitable vesicles. Peer reviewers found the SNAP-tag orientation methodology convincing with no concerns raised, describing evidence as 'solid.'

Both support the PKD2L1 electrophysiology data (C61-C63, C94-C97). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative data, appropriate controls, and reporting of variability. Peer reviewers accepted the conductance measurements without critique, with Peer R4 also including ion selectivity claim C64 that OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

OpenEval R5 addresses ion selectivity (C64) separately as SUPPORTED, noting consistency with prior work. Peer R4 groups this with broader electrophysiology claims (C10, C60-C64, C94-C97) and supports the overall functional characterization including selectivity.

Perfect alignment on PKD2 conductance data (C65-C66, C102-C105). Both evaluations support the claims. OpenEval notes the method generalizes to a second polycystin member with similar conductance patterns. Peer reviewers accepted PKD2 data alongside PKD2L1 with no concerns raised.

Both support the comparison between synthetic and native PKD2L1 channels (C68, C98-C101). OpenEval notes conductance values are remarkably similar with ~10% difference within reasonable variation. Peer reviewers accepted the native channel comparison without concerns, with the editor noting the method allows comparison to endogenous properties.

Both address PKD2 discrepancies (C69, C106-C109). OpenEval supports the documentation of 2-fold higher conductances in synthetic channels as an important limitation. Peer R7 also includes the authors' explanations (C70-C75) and accepts the transparent discussion of limitations, with no reviewer challenging the comparison.

Both support the mechanistic explanations for discrepancies (C70-C75). OpenEval emphasizes the reasonable explanations supported by literature citations and honest assessment of limitations. Peer reviewers accepted the authors' acknowledgment of limitations and interpretation of differences.

Both support the technical limitation regarding GUV instability (C88-C91). OpenEval emphasizes the critical empty GUV control and plausible mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers did not challenge these observations or the over-incorporation hypothesis, consistent with transparent reporting.

Both support the technical limitation and proposed solutions (C81-C82). OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of challenges with reasonable suggestions. Peer R9 groups this with C88-C91 and accepts the transparent reporting, with Reviewer 1 noting concerns were addressed.

Perfect alignment on method generalizability claims (C76-C80). Both evaluations support the claims. OpenEval notes successful application to two channels validates proof-of-principle with reasonable extrapolations. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed broader applicability, with all three reviewers emphasizing potential for studying organellar channels and other difficult targets.

Perfect alignment on forward-looking method extensions (C83-C85). Both evaluations support the claims. OpenEval notes well-supported background with logical extensions and important caveats about chaperone requirements. Peer reviewers did not contest this discussion, consistent with positive assessment of method potential.

OpenEval R14 addresses background/motivation claims (C1-C6) as SUPPORTED, establishing context for the method development. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental claims rather than background literature.

OpenEval R15 addresses methodological approach claims (C34-C36) separately as SUPPORTED background. Peer R1 groups these with protein synthesis data (C47-C52) in a single evaluation, supporting both the CFE-GUV approach and protein production together.

OpenEval R16 addresses background claims on biological/medical significance (C37-C46) as SUPPORTED, establishing why these channels are important validation targets. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental results rather than background context.
